pr_body:
##### Summary
Add a child process reaper to the main netdata app if running as init (pid = 1).

This prevents zombie processes when a child is re-parented to netdata when its running in a container.

Also:
* Few style cleanups to match surrounding code.

Fixes: #6033

##### Component Name
netdata binary

##### Additional Information
This re-purposes old commented out code in `popen.c`, which already implemented part of the required process tracking.

Without this on a standard netdata docker install we saw at least one zombie `timeout` process straight after the container was started.

Manage this branch in Squash

Test this branch here: https://stevenhinit-reaper-k202r.squash.io
@stevenh i would suggest to not force-push w/o reason, it is not clear what is fixed and we have to review from scratch.

Thanks for the feedback so far guys, always good to get to know the nuances of project, no force pushes. 👍 

I've addressed all the feedback, fixing a few other niggles along the way, as well as eliminating some robustness issues which became apparent when stress testing for multiple children exiting; i.e. the data race when setting pid.

issue_context.title: Defunct timeout processes from charts.d plugin in Docker
issue_context.body:
##### Bug report summary
Unable to take actions on system due to inability to fork new processes due to netdata creation of `timeout` defunct processes

##### OS / Environment
Docker, 1.18
Ubuntu 18.04

##### Netdata version (ouput of `netdata -V`)
```
# netdata -V
netdata v1.14.0-11-ge91b9ca
```

##### Component Name
netdata core / charts.d / nut plugin?

##### Steps To Reproduce
Run netdata in docker.
Disable 'apps' plugin.
Enable charts.d plugin for nut, configure nut plugin

```
# cat netdata.conf
[plugins]
  apps = no
```

##### Expected behavior
For netdata to not exhaust kernel of process slots

```
-- The initial discovery of a problem on the system
# docker start grafana
runtime/cgo: pthread_create failed: No space left on device
runtime/cgo: pthread_create failed: No space left on device
SIGABRT: abort
PC=0x7f6c7d022e97 m=3 sigcode=18446744073709551610
...

-- Plus received this alarm from another cron job running
/bin/sh: 1: Cannot fork

-- No space? That's odd.
# df -h /
Filesystem                         Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-ubuntu--lv  5.9G  3.7G  2.0G  66% /

-- No, not a space issue.
-- What is currently running?
# ps -Af
...
201        300 30437  0 00:11 ?        00:00:00 [timeout] <defunct>
201        301 30437  0 May15 ?        00:00:00 [timeout] <defunct>
201        302 30437  0 02:28 ?        00:00:00 [timeout] <defunct>
201        303 30437  0 08:26 ?        00:00:00 [timeout] <defunct>
201        304 30437  0 04:26 ?        00:00:00 [timeout] <defunct>
201        305 30437  0 12:39 ?        00:00:00 [timeout] <defunct>
...(repeated thousands of times)

-- WTH is that?
# ps -Af | grep 30437
201      30437 30412  1 May15 ?        00:14:16 /usr/sbin/netdata -u netdata -D -s /host -p 19999

-- What? Why is netdata spawning so many timeouts and why are they defuncting?

# ps -Af | grep timeout | wc -l
32127

-- Woah! netdata has spawned 32,000 timeouts! Kill it!

# kill -9 30437
# ps -Af | grep timeout
root      2497   817  0 15:27 pts/0    00:00:00 grep timeout

-- Phew! back to normal
```

@ntimo Check out my new script for nut/UPS #6827

I just pushed a fix for the underling problem behind this issue, which was the fact the netdata didn't have a process reaper, see above.

This is only an issue when netdata is run in a container where it must perform the task of the unix `init` process and reap any child processes that have been re-parented to it.

review_comments: I really hate this but I don't see a way around it without rewriting the daemon.
A potential problem here is that all signal handling is effectively blocked until somebody calls `mypclose()`, such as health reload or exiting.

Indeed wasn't a fan either, the only thing I thought of was to have this handled in a separate thread; seems like this could be a future enhancement?

Shame its not in `go` as that would just be a few lines of code, not so simple in `C` though ;-)

Even in `go` I don't think it's guaranteed that `waitid(P_ALL, (id_t)0, &i, WEXITED|WNOHANG|WNOWAIT)` will return any other pid than the one being handled by `myp` which would not allow the loop to iterate.
I actually meant its much easier to throw up a `goroutine` to handle each type of signal, not that it solves the wait issue.
